extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal funding (schools, colleges, K-12 districts), Title IX Coordinators, school administrators, compliance officers, and legal counsel implementing Title IX regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and standards governing what a recipient's Title IX Coordinator must do when notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, including notification, supportive measures, initiation of grievance or informal resolution, and other prompt and effective steps to end and prevent recurrence of sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger: conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: When notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or these regulations, a recipient must require its Title IX Coordinator to take the specific actions described in §106.44(f)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Title IX Coordinator must assess whether the information received reasonably may constitute sex discrimination; if the Title IX Coordinator reasonably determines pursuant to paragraph (f)(2) that the conduct as alleged could not constitute sex discrimination, the actions in (f)(1) are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable treatment of complainant and respondent (§106.44(f)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title IX Coordinator must treat a complainant and respondent equitably, including in communications, to provide information about Title IX policies, available resources, and supports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable treatment applies to parties (complainant and respondent) and does not require treating employee and student respondents identically; it is distinct from grievance-procedure-specific requirements in §106.45(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer and coordination of supportive measures (§106.44(f)(1)(ii) and §106.2 definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must require its Title IX Coordinator to offer and coordinate supportive measures, as appropriate, for a complainant upon notice of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination; and to offer and coordinate supportive measures for a respondent if the recipient has initiated grievance procedures or offered an informal resolution process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures must be non-disciplinary, non-punitive, may not be imposed for punitive reasons, and may not unreasonably burden either party. Supportive measures are subject to limits in §106.44(g)(2) and may be challenged under §106.44(g)(4). The final definition removes language suggesting preliminary determination ('deter the respondent') and removes 'temporary measures that burden a respondent,' replacing it with 'measures that are designed to protect the safety of the parties.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification duties when complainant known or unknown (§106.44(f)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator must notify the complainant (or, if the complainant is unknown, the individual who reported the conduct) of the recipient's grievance procedures and the availability of an informal resolution process if available and appropriate; and must notify a respondent of grievance procedures and informal resolution if a complaint is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing only website links that do not work does not satisfy the obligation. Recipients may require written notification but are not required to do so by these regulations. When complainant is unknown, notifying the reporting individual helps identify the complainant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of grievance procedures or informal resolution (§106.44(f)(1)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title IX Coordinator must initiate a recipient's informal resolution process if available, appropriate, and requested by all parties; and must initiate grievance procedures in accordance with §106.45 (and §106.46 if applicable) when a complainant wishes to initiate a complaint or when directed under the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grievance-procedure requirements apply once a complaint is initiated; the Title IX Coordinator's (f)(1)(i)-(iii) actions help determine when to initiate a complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator-initiated complaint authority (§106.44(f)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title IX Coordinator may initiate a complaint under §106.44(f)(1)(v) after assessing the information received and determining that initiating a complaint is warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Title IX Coordinator initiates a complaint, the Coordinator must provide the respondent information about grievance procedures and informal resolution (if available and appropriate), and disciplinary sanctions may only be imposed after complying with §106.45 (and §106.46 if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to take other appropriate prompt and effective steps regardless of complaint initiation (§106.44(f)(1)(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regardless of whether a complaint is initiated, a recipient must require its Title IX Coordinator to take other appropriate prompt and effective steps, in addition to steps necessary to effectuate remedies provided to an individual complainant, to ensure that sex discrimination does not continue or recur within the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These steps are distinct from remedies to an individual complainant and are limited to non-disciplinary actions when grievance procedures have not been initiated (examples: educational programming, employee training, permitting a complainant to retake a class). Such steps must not be punitive or unreasonably burden a party. If disciplinary sanctions would be required, grievance procedures must be initiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and effective response standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must afford a prompt and effective response to sex discrimination; this standard is longstanding (from 1975 regulations) and consistent with the deliberate indifference standard used by courts and other federal civil rights statutes (e.g., Section 504).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts have found deliberate indifference where there is a 'lengthy and unjustifiable delay' or an 'inadequate or ineffective' response. The Department expects Title IX Coordinators to act promptly and effectively to end discrimination, prevent recurrence, and remedy effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on independent investigation and due process protections
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title IX Coordinator's required actions under §106.44(f) do not authorize the Coordinator to conduct an independent investigation that imposes disciplinary sanctions or circumvents grievance procedures; disciplinary sanctions are permitted only after compliance with grievance-procedure requirements in §106.45 (and §106.46 if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions under §106.44(f)(1)(vii) when grievance procedures are not initiated should be non-disciplinary and not unreasonably burden any party; parties retain rights to challenge supportive measures under §106.44(g)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of offering supportive measures to respondent
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations delay the offer of supportive measures to a respondent until the recipient has initiated grievance procedures or notified the respondent of the availability of an informal resolution process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This timing avoids prematurely notifying the respondent before the complainant decides whether to make a complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for delay for concurrent law enforcement investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may, for good cause, allow reasonable extensions of timeframes (including delaying notification to a respondent) when a concurrent criminal investigation could be negatively impacted, under §§106.45(b)(4) and 106.46(e)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such delays are not required by the regulations but may be justified on a case-by-case basis depending on circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parental notification not mandated by federal Title IX regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in final §106.44(f)(1)(iii) or other provisions requires a Title IX Coordinator to notify the parent, guardian, or other authorized legal representative of a minor; any such duty arises under State/local law or school policy, not these federal regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal regs do not derogate legal rights of parents/guardians to act on behalf of a party where state or local law or policy provides that authority (see §106.6(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must train, permit delegation, and comply with expanded Title IX Coordinator role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department expects recipients to adequately train Title IX Coordinators to distinguish allegations that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination from allegations that could not constitute sex discrimination, to permit Title IX Coordinators to delegate duties, and to comply with expanded reporting and Coordinator responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department will offer technical assistance as appropriate; recipients are expected to ensure Title IX Coordinators and employees are equipped to comply, including by imposing additional training requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient compliance and discretion: 'doing nothing' is not inherently required nor always wrong
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient would not be in compliance if its Title IX Coordinator failed to take any of the required steps under §106.44(f)(1); however, if the Title IX Coordinator reasonably assesses the information and determines no further action is warranted, the recipient may be in compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples when no additional steps are necessary: discrimination involved only the parties and did not impact others and was addressed fully through grievance procedures or informal resolution; or complainant pursued remedies under a collective bargaining agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures: challengeability and prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures may be challenged under §106.44(g)(4), are subject to limits in §106.44(g)(2), and may not be imposed for punitive or disciplinary reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final definition clarifies supportive measures balance supporting complainants and ensuring respondents are not disciplined absent a finding of responsibility; many supportive measures will not burden a party at all.
